definitions.explanation: Substances that are not derived from living organisms and generally do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds. Includes minerals, metals, water, and salts. The opposite of organic matter (有機物).

examples.japanese: {水|みず}は{無機物|むきぶつ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Water is one type of inorganic substance.

examples.japanese: {岩石|がんせき}は{無機物|むきぶつ}でできている。
examples.english: Rocks are made of inorganic matter.

examples.japanese: {理科|りか}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{有機物|ゆうきぶつ}と{無機物|むきぶつ}の{違|ちが}いを{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: I learned the difference between organic and inorganic matter in science class.

notes:
FORMS:
{無機|むき} (inorganic) + {物|ぶつ} (matter, substance). {無機|むき} is {無|む} (without) + {機|き} (mechanism/organic), referring to things without the complex structures of living organisms.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有機物|ゆうきぶつ}: organic matter

SIMILAR COMPOUNDS:
- {無機質|むきしつ}: inorganic (also figuratively: cold, impersonal)
- {鉱物|こうぶつ}: mineral

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無機物|むきぶつ}と{有機物|ゆうきぶつ}: inorganic and organic matter
- {無機|むき}{化合物|かごうぶつ}: inorganic compound
